en: When plant roots absorb water, it travels up the stem and evaporates through leaf stomata, pulling more water upward.
When the diaphragm muscle contracts and moves downward, it increases chest cavity volume, causing air to rush into the lungs.
Bats emit high-frequency sound waves that bounce off flying insects, allowing the bat to locate its prey in complete darkness.
When a virus enters the body, white blood cells produce specific antibodies that bind to and neutralize the invading pathogen.
If a predator like the wolf is removed from an ecosystem, the herbivore population explodes and overgrazes the available plants.
Cacti store water in their thick stems and have modified spines instead of leaves to minimize water loss in deserts.
During a frog's metamorphosis, the tadpole's gills are replaced by lungs, and its tail is absorbed into the body for energy.
Salivary glands release amylase enzymes into the mouth, which chemically break down complex starches into simpler sugars during chewing.
Dogs pant to evaporate moisture from their tongues and lungs, which cools their blood and lowers their body temperature.
Plant stems bend toward light because the hormone auxin accumulates on the shaded side, causing those cells to elongate faster.
Fungi secrete enzymes that break down dead organic matter, releasing essential nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil for plants.
Vaccines introduce weakened pathogens to train the immune system, prompting it to produce memory cells that fight future infections faster.
